newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND SHORTLISTS TWO BIDDERS FOR MOTORWAY SCHEME.
newsitem.headline: POLAND SHORTLISTS TWO BIDDERS FOR MOTORWAY SCHEME.

text.p: Poland has shortlisted Gdansk Transport Company SA and Euroute Polska SA for the second phase of a tender for building a stretch of the country's motorway scheme, the transport ministry's spokeswoman said.
Teresa Jarmulowicz told Reuters that the consortia bid for building a 150-kilometer span of the A1 motorway to link the northern city of Gdansk and Torun in central Poland.
"The government commission chose Gdansk Transport Company SA and Euroute Polska SA for the second stage of the tender," Jarmulowicz told Reuters.
Gdansk Transport Company includes the city's road management, Bank Gdanski , the Gdansk municipality, Zasada and Bechtel International.
Euroute includes German Bilfinger plus Berger Bau AG Mannheim and Spanish Dragados y Construciones SA.
Poland plans to build 2,500 kilometers of toll expressways over the next 15 years.

Under the programme, passed by parliament in 1994, consortia of Polish and foreign firms are invited to public tenders to build sections of motorways, where they will be allowed to collect tolls for 25 to 30 years.
The total cost of the construction is estimated at $8 billion.
